COLORS LESSON · COLORS & SHADES · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Red — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the color red: what it is, where it hides, and how to hunt it.

What is this?

Red is a color — the color of the apple, the fire truck, the ladybug and the strawberry on the card. Colors are words for how things LOOK, and red is usually the very first color word a child learns.

What does it mean?

Red is the color that shouts: stop signs are red, fire trucks are red, ripe strawberries are red. Your brain learned "red means look at me" long before you had a word for it.

What does the child need to know?

The child needs to: say "red", point at red things, and sort red from not-red. Four red things on the card is four repetitions of the same word — that is how the word sticks.

Why this matters

Color words are classification — the first science a child does. Naming red is sorting the world into groups, and sorting is the skill behind counting, reading and tidying up.

What it teaches

Vocabulary (one loud word, four anchors), visual discrimination (red versus not-red), and categorizing — the same muscle that sorts socks and letters later.

Words to learn

redapplefire truckladybugstrawberryhuntfindmatchspotsort

Say this to your child

“"Red! Say it loud — RED. The apple is red, the truck is red, the ladybug is red, the strawberry is red. Red is the color that says LOOK AT ME. Ready to hunt? First one to find something red gets a strawberry!"”

Step by step

  1. Hold the card up and point at each square, saying the word: apple — red, fire truck — red, ladybug — red, strawberry — red.
  2. Ask your child to point: "where is the red fire truck?" Then swap: they ask, you point (get one wrong on purpose — being the teacher is thrilling).
  3. The red hunt: walk the house and find five red things together. Count them out loud on the way.
  4. Snack the lesson: a strawberry or apple slice, named red before the first bite. Colors you eat stick deepest.
  5. Close by flipping the question: "what is NOT red on this card?" Trick question — everything is red! Laugh, then spot one not-red thing in the room.

Look closer at the picture

Look at the card closely: all four squares are different KINDS of red things — a fruit you eat, a truck that races, a bug that crawls, a berry you pick. One word covers them all. That is what color words can do.

Ask your child

"Which red thing on the card can fly?" (ladybug — well, flutter!) "Which red thing has a ladder?" (fire truck) "Which red thing do we eat?" (apple and strawberry)

What your child can say or do

Your child might start calling every round red thing "a strawberry" for a week, or point at the fire truck square and make the siren noise. Both are the lesson working.

Out in the real world

Fire trucks are red in the US, the UK and Canada — and the stop sign is red on three continents. The card’s reds are the ones your child will meet out the front door.

Try it together

Red light, green light, card edition: hold the red card up — everyone freezes. (The green lesson will bring the running. For now: freeze, giggle, freeze.)

Understanding check

Ask: "what color is the fire truck?" (red!) "Find something red in this room." (the hunt says it worked) "Is the sky red?" (no — silly, and sillies are learning)

This lesson pairs with the Red flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shades.
